newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE PLANS 15PCT TAX ON GAINS ON DERIVATIVES.
newsitem.headline: GREECE PLANS 15PCT TAX ON GAINS ON DERIVATIVES.

text.p: Greece plans to introduce a 15 percent tax on income and gains from derivatives, trading in currency and interest rate swaps, FRAs and options, according to a new draft bill.
Deputy Finance minister George Drys has prepared a draft bill which, according to news reports, has the backing of the Bank of Greece and the Union of Hellenic Banks.

The bill, expected to be submitted to parliament soon, states that gains from derivatives trades will be subject to a 15 percent tax witholding both for individual, corporate and institutional investors. The tax will be the only tax liability on income or gains realised on these transactions.

According to the bill, excluded from the 15 percent tax will be trades between credit institutions and non-Greek residents. Also, losses resulting from derivatives trading may be used as a tax exemption.
Dealers noted that the derivatives market in Greece was just starting to pick up.
The tax would have an impact on hedgers, imposing an extra cost on their efforts to shield from currency or interest rate risks, a dealer said. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
